newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to decide on N.Korea food aid in 24 hours.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to decide on N.Korea food aid in 24 hours.

text.p: The United States on Monday promised an announcement within 24 hours on whether it would provide new food aid to famine-stricken North Korea.

"The United States is now finishing its internal deliberations on the issue of whether or not to respond to the augmented appeal of the World Food Programme for a greater level of food assistance to North Korea, and I would expect within the next 24 hours that I will have an announcement to make on that issue," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
The World Food Programme has called for $95.5 million for 200,000 tons of food. Washington has provided $18.4 million since late 1995, including a $10 million donation now being shipped to Pyongyang.
Burns said the United States and North Korea had also agreed to hold talks in New York May 12-13 to discuss U.S. concerns over North Korea's reported exports of missiles.
He told a news briefing that a U.S. team led by Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Robert Einhorn wanted to discuss reports of "various allegations of sales and transfers."

Before that, the United States hopes to receive at a meeting in New York Wednesday with North and South Korean officals a response from Pyongyang to a U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-way talks on the future of Korea. Burns reiterated U.S. denials that the food aid was being used to elicit a positive response from North Korea.
